summary.title: Design patterns for microservices
summary.one_liner: Nine Azure Architecture Center patterns (such as Ambassador, Bulkhead, Gateway Routing and Strangler) for solving common problems when designing microservices.
keywords: how to split monolith into microservices
takeaways: Nine patterns are listed: Ambassador, Anti-corruption layer, Backends for Frontends, Bulkhead, Gateway Aggregation, Gateway Offloading, Gateway Routing, Sidecar, and Strangler.
Gateway patterns (Aggregation, Offloading, Routing) reduce chattiness and endpoint sprawl between clients and services.
Bulkhead isolates resources per workload so one service cannot starve others and cause cascading failures.
Strangler supports incremental migration by replacing functionality piece by piece with new services.
For each pattern the source describes the problem, solution, when to use it, and implementation considerations (full detail is on the Architecture Center).
summary.summary: This Azure blog post announces nine new design patterns from the AzureCAT patterns & practices team, published on the Azure Architecture Center, aimed at microservices. It gives a one-line description of each pattern, covering client connectivity offloading, legacy integration, client-specific backends, resource isolation, gateway behaviours, helper containers, and incremental migration. The post says each pattern is documented with problem, solution, when to use, and implementation considerations, but those details are on the linked Architecture Center pages rather than in this post.
